The accused/applicants seek anticipatory bail in case FIR No. 109/2025 of Police Station Saket,
South Delhi for offence under Section 420/468/471/34 of IPC.

3. Broadly speaking, the allegation against the accused/applicants is that the complainant de facto executed an agreement/Memorandum of Understanding dated 04.07.2017 and mortgaged her immovable property for obtaining loan of Rs. 25,00,000/- from the accused/applicants, out of which she paid back Rs.13,77,000/- and assured to pay back the entire balance within five years Yagya Dutt Sharma vs The State Of Nct Of Delhi on 30 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/135532532/

sentences.text: But the accused/applicants Shweta Sharma and her husband Yagya Dutt Sharma violated the MoU and sold away the subject property to one Vijay Singh Kamal and Shashank Kamal.
4. Learned counsel for accused/applicants contends that what was only a civil dispute has been given colour of criminality only to pressurize the accused/applicants.

It is also contended that the complainant de facto had sold the subject property to the accused Shweta Sharma by way of registered sale deed, so there was no illegality in the accused persons selling away the same to Vijay Singh Kamal and Shashank Kamal.
It is further submitted that despite passage of nine years, no civil suit has been instituted by the complainant de facto against the accused/applicants.

Learned counsel for accused/applicants also takes me through order dated 23.03.2026 whereby the earlier anticipatory bail applications were dismissed in default, but the accused/applicants were granted liberty to file fresh applications and in This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 30/03/2026 at 22:44:12 those anticipatory bail applications, the accused/applicants were granted interim protection from arrest.
5. Learned APP for State assisted by IO/SI Karan Singh accepts notice.
6. Complainant de facto, identified by the IO also, is present and is informed that she has a right to be heard.
The complainant de facto submits that she has no money to engage a counsel.
She is apprised of her right to file application for free legal aid and has been informed the office address of DHCLSC.

However, the complainant de facto also alleges that the parties had clearly agreed that after she pays back the entire loan amount, the subject property would be transferred back to the complainant de facto since the sale was by way of security.
7. The status report be filed within four weeks.
8. Till next date, the accused/applicants shall not be arrested.
9. Relist on 21.07.2026 in Advance List.
GIRISH KATHPALIA, J MARCH 30, 2026/
